projects.name: SparkFlow
projects.blurb: BitBang's in-house, Jira-style project-management platform — boards, sprints, reporting and test management, with an MCP server that hands tickets to AI agents.
projects.problem: Several of us — me included — were between client projects. I pitched turning that bench time into a product BitBang could use: one place to plan, track and test delivery work, with Microsoft sign-in, strict project isolation and QA tied to the same issues.
projects.solution: I gathered the features, wrote the requirements, and designed the database (ERDs), its security and the UI/UX, then built it with AI-assisted development: a NestJS (Fastify) API over PostgreSQL and Prisma, Redis-backed realtime and BullMQ jobs, and a React frontend — workspaces, boards, backlog, sprints, a rich-text editor with mentions, dashboards, reports and native test management. It also ships an MCP server: developers create tickets in bulk and hand them to AI agents, which move each ticket's status when the work is done, so SparkFlow plugs straight into AI-assisted workflows.
projects.decision: Design first, then build fast: the requirements, ERDs and a security model with tenant and project isolation enforced in the database came before any code, and AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Design) kept the build fast. I then kept redesigning it from the teams' feedback until it was good enough to replace Jira outright.
projects.impact: Replaced BitBang's Jira subscription — every team project now runs on it, with minimal issues since launch, backed by 94 data models and 600+ automated test files.

projects.name: Yally
projects.blurb: An AI workplace platform — documents, chat, calendar, meetings and compliance in one Arabic/English workspace.
projects.problem: Organisations wanted one bilingual workspace where documents, chat, meetings and compliance live together — with AI that can work across all of it.
projects.solution: Full-stack work across the React web app and the C#/.NET (ABP, EF Core) backend: Word 97–2003 files viewable and editable through a .docx rendition, realtime chat events, one set of access rules for attachments, billing and storage-limit rules, and user, role and permission management — plus reliable recording and Arabic, English and mixed-language transcription for its Microsoft Teams meeting bot.
projects.decision: Converted legacy .doc files in a short-lived, capped child process, so one bad file can never block other requests — and pushed realtime chat events only after the database commit, so nobody sees a message that was rolled back.
projects.impact: Closed a full QA release pass across documents, calendar, compliance, billing and user management, and added Arabic and mixed-language meeting transcription.

projects.name: GoPay
projects.blurb: A SADAD-integrated B2B billing and collections platform for Saudi Arabia — public site, operator dashboard and customer apps.
projects.problem: Businesses across regulated Saudi sectors needed one place to issue invoices, collect through every local channel, stay ZATCA-compliant, and see their cash flow — without stitching tools together.
projects.solution: The GoPay frontend, end to end: the marketing site plus the operator dashboard — one-time and recurring payments, invoicing (GoInvoice / ZATCA), reconciliations and approvals — wired to mada, Apple Pay, Visa, Mastercard and SADAD.
projects.decision: Rebuilt GoPay's legacy, hard-to-scale frontend on a feature-based architecture instead of patching it, and set the standards every developer on the team builds on — the most important change I made to the product.
projects.impact: Trusted by leading Saudi organisations — including the Royal Commission for AlUla, the Gulf Health Council and Tawzea Aquapor.

projects.name: Amplifidor
projects.blurb: A two-sided influencer × brand platform — brands launch affiliate programs; creators, agents and agencies join, promote them and get paid per milestone.
projects.problem: Brands wanted to work with creators on measurable terms. Creators — and the agents and agencies who manage them — needed one profile that proves their reach, a way into paid programs, and payouts tied to real results.
projects.solution: A React and TypeScript frontend over a GraphQL API (Apollo, 126 typed operations). I led the frontend and a team of two engineers — set its feature-based architecture and shared component layer, split the work and reviewed every change — and built the creator profile and link-in-bio, the per-platform audience insights and the SAR wallet, plus the English / Arabic localization with full RTL.
projects.decision: Set up a feature-based architecture and a strict review loop aimed at pixel-perfect output, so two engineers could ship in parallel without the UI drifting. The frontend consistently delivered faster than the project's mobile and backend teams.
projects.impact: One bilingual codebase serving four account types — creators, agents, brands and agencies — with 1,500+ interface strings in English and Arabic.

projects.name: Shamel360
projects.blurb: Shamel360's warehouse fulfillment portal — inbound receiving, outbound picking and shipping, live inventory, products and merchants in one console.
projects.problem: Fulfillment teams holding stock for many merchants needed one console for the whole flow: receiving inbound shipments, picking and dispatching orders through last-mile carriers, and tracking every merchant's stock as it moves through the warehouse.
projects.solution: A React 19 and TypeScript portal over a REST API (TanStack Query, Zustand, Radix / shadcn, Tailwind): a configurable dashboard, inbound and outbound boards that follow every order's status, inventory, products, merchants and finance. I rebuilt it from scratch with a new UI, led three developers, and built the hardest components — collapsible table column groups, virtualized tables and a Jira-style board — plus the inventory and product-approval flows.
projects.decision: A feature-based architecture in a monorepo, with one shared UI package for the fulfillment and merchant portals, so complex components are built once and reused; virtualization keeps very large tables fast.
projects.impact: One console for the full fulfillment loop across multiple warehouses — 38 routes over nearly 100 API endpoints, built on the routing, layout and shared components I set up.

projects.name: WalaPlus
projects.blurb: A loyalty and employee-rewards platform for Saudi enterprises — points, offers and cashback across a network of real retail brands.
projects.problem: Enterprises needed to run points, rewards, offers and cashback for thousands of employees and family accounts — across dozens of merchants — from one admin, in Arabic and English.
projects.solution: As the company's sole frontend developer, I modernized every product's frontend onto a current stack and built this bilingual (RTL / LTR) admin: customizable dashboards, points-pool management, reward catalogs, retailer and offer administration, employee invites by email or file, and reports on transactions, points and savings.
projects.decision: Rebuilt the legacy, server-rendered Blade PHP client portal as a modern SPA, then moved the company's other products onto the same modern stack — working across almost every product and supporting hiring along the way.
projects.impact: A platform tracking 2.8B+ loyalty points across 114 retailers — including LandMark, HungerStation and Careem.

projects.name: Fatura
projects.blurb: A B2B wholesale-ordering and credit platform for FMCG distribution — including the operation that runs Coca-Cola’s distribution in Egypt.
projects.problem: Distributors, operations, auditors, collectors and retail clients each needed their own workflow over one shared catalog, order flow and credit ledger.
projects.solution: A shared React / TypeScript / Vue frontend with role-specific portals — orders & transactions, a catalog and ad-campaign builder, and BelAgel credit collections. My part: I delivered the React credit-service portal, built the internal Audit Portal in React and TypeScript, implemented the Vue Collector Portal, and took backend tasks in Node / Express: Google social login, API changes and database migrations.
projects.impact: Diagnosed and fixed a major performance issue in the Operations Portal's transaction filters, cutting wait times by ~80% for a portal serving thousands of clients.

projects.name: Møller Auto
projects.blurb: The used-car marketplace for Volkswagen and Audi’s official dealer network across the Baltics.
projects.problem: Hundreds of live cars across a multi-country dealer network — each with deep specs, pricing, leasing and reservation flows — all needing to load fast and stay legible.
projects.solution: A performant listing and detail experience on Magento: faceted search over 800+ cars, spec-dense car pages, a leasing calculator, trade-in, and a dealership locator spanning Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania. I owned most of the storefront's frontend and the styling of its CMS pages.

about.label: About
about.heading: A senior engineer who cares about the parts users ==don't== see.
paragraphs: I'm a full-stack engineer with a frontend-first bias, drawn to the unglamorous half of the job — the data models, the API contracts, the component contracts, the performance budgets. The work that decides whether a product feels solid six months after launch, or starts to rot.

For **six-plus years** I've shipped fintech dashboards, admin portals, and design-system-driven apps — and lately the C#/.NET and Node services behind them, plus AI features like meeting transcription. I translate ambiguous designs into clean interfaces, raise the floor through reviews and standards, and use *AI tooling daily* as a multiplier — while owning every decision that ships.

experience.label: Experience
experience.heading: Six years, across fintech, platforms & operations.

Owns the GoPay frontend, led the Amplifidor and Shamel360 frontend teams, and initiated SparkFlow, the in-house platform that replaced the company's Jira. Leads and mentors engineers and sets the standards that keep delivery fast and maintainable.

A demo of Chapter I of The Last Abbasid, a 2D pixel-art action game set in Baghdad in 1258, is out on itch.io in English and Arabic; the full game is planned for Steam.

The company's sole frontend developer: modernized every product's frontend and built the WalaPlus loyalty & rewards admin — bilingual dashboards, points pools, reward catalogs and reporting — for enterprise employee-loyalty programs across Saudi retail brands.

Built ordering, operations, audit and collector portals — plus the BelAgel credit-collections system — on a shared React, TypeScript and Vue frontend, and took backend tasks in Node/Express: Google social login, API changes and migration scripts. The platform also powered Coca-Cola’s distribution operations in Egypt.

Frontend delivery on large-scale Magento e-commerce alongside a distributed team — the Møller Auto marketplace (VW & Audi) and the Printerbase storefront, owning most of their frontend and CMS styling.
Built the Andalusia Care site in Nuxt to improve patient access to healthcare services and information.
Started in mobile with Flutter — a reservation app that passed 1,000+ downloads, and a foundation in cross-platform UI that still informs how I design for multiple surfaces.

principles.label: How I think
principles.heading: Software that ==lasts==.
principles.intro: Everything below is in service of one idea: code that the next engineer — or future me — can pick up and move forward without flinching.

items.title: Data and contracts first
items.description: ERDs, typed API contracts and access rules settled before the UI. When the shape of the data is right, the screens mostly follow.

items.title: Component architecture
items.description: Composable components with clear boundaries and predictable APIs, extracted once and reused everywhere. The shape of the code should make the wrong thing awkward to write.

items.title: Design systems & tokens
items.description: Tokens, themes, and docs that keep the UI consistent and themable — so change is a variable, not a refactor.

items.title: Correct under failure
items.description: Side effects after the commit, idempotent jobs, and slow work that can't block anyone else. Systems should fail small and recover on their own.

items.title: Performance
items.description: Real budgets and measured metrics. Rendering that stays smooth under the load that actually ships.

items.title: Reviews & standards
items.description: Reviews that raise the floor, not the ego, and tooling that makes the whole team faster. Readable, tested, maintainable code as the default.
